title: Email triage: how much of each body to send
summary: 50 made-up emails, each classified 5 times at each cut (the first 600, 1,000, 1,500, 2,000, 3,000 and 4,000 characters and the whole body) by Claude Haiku through the dashboard's own classify.llm_verdicts. Before: the first 600 characters of each body, as the dashboard sends today. After: the whole body.
legend: Calendar entries that shouldn't exist: 0 before, 0 after (across all repeats). Rates count only the cases where a field applies: dates caught is over emails that need a calendar entry.

work-confirmed-zoom (before): The deciding text ends at character 4228, but the classifier only sends the first 600, so the model never saw it.

work-invite-short (before): The email has an explicit date and time, but the classifier dropped it because it clashed with another email in the batch, and the instructions never say how to treat conflicting or related emails.

work-reschedule (before): The instructions say a time that might still move gets lower certainty rather than null, but they don't say what to do when a reschedule asks for confirmation and clashes with another email, so the model chose null.
work-invite-ats-relative (after): Received on Friday 2 Oct, 'next Thursday' could mean 8 or 15 Oct, and the instructions say to return null when in doubt, so the gold's confident 8 Oct is arguable.

work-confirmed-zoom (after): The interview is 20 days away and the instructions put 'appointment confirmations further out' under important, so IMPORTANT is defensible even though 'interview invitations' are listed under super.
